messages.subject: NN matching
messages.body_plain:
Howdy,
I have a question regarding NN matching.  My call looks as follows:
matchit(match.f.2,p.2,method="nearest",distance="logit",ratio=1,caliper=.1)->m.nc.2
In the documentation, the m.order defaults to "largest" so the treated
units are paired up from the highest value of the distance to the
lowest.  I've run this a number of times and gotten different results
every time; my first thought was that the controls were randomly
arranged each time such that a different match is being made.  Looking
at the matchit2nearest source (which I haven't completely deciphered)
makes me not so sure about that idea.  What is going on here?  And is
there a way to "fix" this option such that the same match is made
every time (specifically, it's making a certain sweave document
difficult to write when things keep changing).
Thanks for any advice,
Ben

messages.subject: Re: NN matching
messages.body_plain:
Ben, I'm not sure why it would give different
answers each time, but I'd guess its your inputs; are you creating them
by simulation perhaps?  if so, you can set the random seed and you'll
get the same answer every time.

Gary

messages.subject: Re: NN matching
messages.body_plain:
I think you could also get different answers if you have some ties (i.e., individuals with the same propensity scores)--in that case I believe MatchIt will pick the match randomly from among those with the same values.  I would hope that the results are not that different from different runs; if so, that implies the results are probably quite sensitive to small changes to the procedure.

In any case, if you want to ensure getting the same result each time, you can use the set.seed() command, as Gary mentioned.

Liz

messages.subject: Re: NN matching
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the advice.  The data is not random, so perhaps it does
have to do with ties.
I also wanted to mention something that I've brought up before
(http://lists.gking.harvard.edu/lists/matchit/2008_11/msg00001.html),
but I realized today it is still a problem.  When you call match.data
from a function, things seem to go wrong.  The problem is, I think,
that the first line of match.data
  data <- eval(object$call$data)
fails when the environment isn't the global environment.  I've gotten
match.data to work in a function by redefining a match.data.star
function with the following modification to the first line:
  #data <- eval(object$call$data)
  get(as.character(object$call$data),sys.frame(1))->data
It's kind of a kludge, but this is at least a problem that people
should be aware of.
Ben

messages.subject: Re: Problem with Memory when I'm running MatchIt
messages.subject_clean: Problem with Memory when I'm running MatchIt
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

   I'm ccing your message to the MatchIt mailserve to which any questions 
should be directed.

   The memory problem is not specific to MatchIt, but is a general issue 
using R.  If you are using a Windows machine, I believe that you can 
follow the instruction given here; 
http://gking.harvard.edu/zelig/docs/static/faq.pdf

   If you are using a 64 bit Mac/Unix machine, then you might consider 
optimizing R.  I did it following http://r.research.att.com/ and it worked 
well for me.

   The last resort, which might be the easiest, would be to subset the data 
by matching exactly on the discrete covariate and then do further matching 
within that subset of the data.

Best,
Kosuke

-- 
Department of Politics
Princeton University
